Article Text:
Fadnavis said people deserved clarity on what had happened.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis on Monday urged Union home minister Amit Shah to expedite the investigation into the plane crash that killed former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar and make the findings public at the earliest.Speaking at a programme in Pune where Shah unveiled a bust of the late NCP leader at the Pune Zilla Parishad (ZP) office, Fadnavis said, "Eight to 10 months have passed, and a major investigation is underway. Teams from different countries and international agencies are also assisting in the probe. However, the confusion and apprehensions in the minds of ordinary people in Maharashtra must be addressed. The investigation report should come out at the earliest. "Raising questions about the circumstances of the crash, the chief minister said people deserved clarity on what had happened and called for strict action if anyone was found guilty."People want to know what exactly happened. Was it an accident or was there something else behind it? If anyone is found guilty, they must be given the strictest punishment. And if it was an accident, the anguish and questions in the minds of ordinary people must at least be addressed."Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by VSR Ventures crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport. The aircraft was flying from Mumbai to Baramati. Four others were also killed in the crash.The Maharashtra CID and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the Union civil aviation ministry, are conducting separate investigations into the incident.Following Ajit Pawar's death, his wife Sunetra Pawar took over as the NCP president and became Maharashtra's deputy chief minister.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis said people deserved clarity on what had happened. Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by VSR Ventures crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport. Four others were also killed in the crash.

Article Title: 'When CM was unavailable, Ajit Pawar was there': Amit Shah remembers ex-Maharashtra deputy CM
Article Text:
“Dada's sudden passing away is an irreparable loss”: Amit Shah pays tribute to Ajit Pawar at statue unveiling in Pune

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Monday described the death of former Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar as an “irreparable loss” to the state. He further praised his work ethic and understanding of governance would serve as a “university” for future generations of political leaders.Shah made the remarks after unveiling a bust of Pawar at the Zilla Parishad office premises in Pune, in the presence of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.“The sudden and untimely passing away of 'Dada' is an irreparable loss, not only for Maharashtra, but specifically for the regions of Pune, Baramati, Pimpri and Chinchwad,” Shah said.He added that the void left by Pawar's death could not be filled even with collective efforts over several decades. The bust, he said, would inspire future generations to learn from the late leader's work and contributions.Recalling his association with Pawar, Shah described him as a close friend and colleague who had a deep understanding of development, Panchayati Raj, cooperatives, agriculture and urban development.“I found Ajit Pawar very clear and straightforward in all political negotiations,” Shah said.He also praised Pawar's role during the Covid-19 pandemic, taking a swipe at the administration led by then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.Shah said there was no communication with Thackeray during the crisis, but Pawar remained accessible over the landline at the state secretariat and ensured that the government's relief work continued, as quoted by PTI.Describing Pawar as an “encyclopaedia” of the cooperative sector, Shah said his knowledge extended to sugar factories, milk unions, primary agricultural credit societies and cooperative banks, as well as their administrative challenges.Shah also credited Pawar's entry into the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance with helping stabilise the ruling coalition in Maharashtra. Pawar, along with several NCP leaders, had joined the alliance in July 2023, triggering a vertical split in the party then headed by Sharad Pawar.The Union minister said Pawar had made a significant contribution to the transformation of Baramati, his constituency and the Pawar family's political stronghold in Pune district.Meanwhile, CM Fadnavis requested Shah to expedite the investigation into the plane crash that killed Pawar and sought the release of the final report. The Maharashtra CID and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the civil aviation ministry, are conducting separate inquiries into the crash.Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when the aircraft carrying him crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport in Pune district.
Article Summary: Ajit Pawar died on January 28 this year when the aircraft carrying him crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport in Pune district. Union home minister Amit Shah on Monday described the death of former Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar as an “irreparable loss” to the state.

NEW DELHI: A political row has erupted in West Bengal after Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Kalyan Banerjee criticised the BJP government over arrangements for Chhath Puja , alleging that the state had been “taken over” by non-Bengalis and accusing the ruling party of undermining Bengali culture.Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Banerjee questioned the scale of decorations at Howrah railway station for the festival, alleging that similar arrangements were not made for Durga Puja.“Are there Bengalis in West Bengal anymore? Does West Bengal belong to Bengalis or rogue Biharis? Does practising Sanatan dharma mean cutting off Bengalis and establishing Biharis? BJP will destroy the Bengali culture. I was surprised to see Howrah station decked up like that for Chhath. Such decorations are not put up for Durga Puja,” he said, as quoted by news agency ANI.The TMC leader further alleged that Bengalis had become “second-category citizens” in the state and warned that they would “cease to exist” if the situation continued for another five years.His remarks drew a sharp response from West Bengal minister Indranil Khan, who accused the TMC of pursuing divisive politics and questioned its record on issues concerning Bengali culture and people.Khan alleged that neither the previous TMC government nor the Left government had adequately served the interests of Bengali people.“Is it Bengali culture to carry Maa Kali on a prison van? Is it Bengali culture to stop Durga Visarjan for Muharram? Was it in the interest of Bengalis to fire bullets on students demanding the appointment of a teacher for Bengali language at Daribhit? They do divisive politics and nothing else. Had they worked in the interest of Bengalis, 15 years of TMC rule and 34 years of Left rule would have made something good out of Bengal,” he said.Defending the arrangements for Chhath Puja, the minister said people from different communities and cultural backgrounds contributed to the country and had the right to celebrate their festivals.“Ek Bharat Shresht Bharat. People of various diversities contribute towards the country...Everyone has the right to participate in their festival, and it is the duty of the government to stand with them. But TMC and Left didn't do their duty,” Khan said.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari also defended the government's arrangements for the festival, describing Chhath as a celebration of the Sanatan tradition and rejecting attempts to associate it exclusively with any one community or state.Adhikari participated in Chhath Puja celebrations at Ramkrishnapur Ghat in Howrah on Sunday. He said at least one crore followers of the Sanatan tradition were observing the festival and that participation was not limited to Hindi speakers.“At least one crore followers of the Sanatan tradition are observing this. It is not just Hindi speakers; all followers of the Sanatan tradition are participating in Chhath—a grand festival of faith and tradition,” he told reporters.He said the government had made arrangements for Chhath along the lines of preparations for Durga Puja, Kali Puja and Diwali, adding that the facilities for the festival were well organised.Adhikari also accused critics of indulging in “vote-bank appeasement politics” and described their approach as narrow-minded.“They would claim that the Ganpati festival belongs only to the Marathis, that Chhath belongs only to the people of Bihar, or that Ram Navami belongs only to Uttar Pradesh,” he said, adding that people had rejected such divisions and made it clear that “at the end of the day, we are all Indians”.The political exchanges came as devotees across the country marked the final day of the four-day Chhath festival by offering 'arghya' to the rising Sun.Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to devotees on Monday, saying the festival brought together steadfast resolve and spiritual practice.In a post on X, he said, “Today, the four-day ritual of the grand festival of Chhath concluded with the offering of prayers to the rising sun. This divine festival dedicated to nature witnessed a remarkable confluence of steadfast resolve and spiritual practice. I pray to Chhathi Maiya to bestow her blessings on all the devotees observing the fast, as well as on my family members across the country.”Political leaders also participated in celebrations in several states. In Bihar, BJP national president Nitin Nabin was seen carrying a 'daura' as his wife performed the rituals in Patna, while chief minister Samrat Chaudhary offered prayers at a ghat in Munger.In Chhattisgarh, Chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai and his wife participated in the rituals in Kunkuri, where a groundbreaking ceremony for a Chhath Ghat was also held. BJP MP Ravi Kishan offered morning prayers in Gorakhpur, while party MP Manoj Tiwari participated in the celebrations at Sonia Vihar Ghat in Delhi.
Article Summary: TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee accuses ruling party of undermining Bengali culture. West Bengal minister Indranil Khan accuses TMC of pursuing divisive politics. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari defends the government's arrangements for the festival.

NEW DELHI: Italian legislator Deborah Bergamini has criticised Giacomo Filibeck, secretary general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), over his “Vote thieves, step down from your seats” remark targeting the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), saying foreign political representatives should not intervene in the domestic political debate of a friendly country.In a post on X, Bergamini said India had its own political institutions and judiciary to address domestic political disputes. She also pointed to the special strategic partnership between Italy and India, arguing that it was inappropriate for European representatives to lecture the country on democracy.Deborah Bergamini is a member and national deputy secretary of Forza Italia, a centre-right political party that is part of the governing coalition supporting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.Her remarks came after Filibeck, while attending the Bharat Summit 2026 organised by the Congress in Hyderabad, accused the BJP-led government of undermining democracy and expressed support for Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and the Congress.“An Italian representative from the European Socialists and Democrats group, while attending a meeting organised by the Indian National Congress party , attacked Prime Minister Modi’s BJP, declaring: ‘Vote thieves, step down from your seats.’This stems from the Indian opposition’s criticism of the ruling majority regarding a long-overdue revision of electoral rolls—a process intended to remove duplicate entries, the names of deceased individuals, and those who have relocated,” Bergamini said.The revision of electoral rolls has been a point of contention between the opposition and the BJP-led government.“I believe that, in a democracy, everyone is free to put forward whatever arguments or accusations they see fit—provided, of course, that they can substantiate them,” she added.Bergamini said Italy and India shared a “special strategic partnership”, with cooperation across several sectors, and argued that foreign representatives should refrain from intervening in India's internal political discussions.“Furthermore, in instances like this, it is inappropriate to intervene in the domestic political debate of a major friendly nation—a country with which our own has established a ‘special strategic partnership,’ fostering deep cooperation across all sectors,” she said.She also questioned the appropriateness of European representatives commenting on India's democratic processes, citing the scale of its electorate.“Moreover, as Europeans, we find it inappropriate to lecture on democracy a nation that enables 970 million citizens to cast their votes. India possesses its own political institutions and judiciary; any conflicts or disputes should be addressed and resolved in accordance with the established rules of democracy,” Bergamini said.Filibeck had said that international gatherings were important to draw global attention to what he described as challenges facing Indian democracy.“Democracy is under attack in India, and we need to defend it, and the best way to defend it is to stand by Rahul Gandhi and the Indian Congress Party,” he told news agency ANI on the sidelines of the summit.He also said the PES, the Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy.The remarks drew criticism from BJP leaders. BJP national spokesperson and national media co-in-charge Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress MP of seeking foreign interference in India's domestic political affairs.In a post on X, Bhandari alleged that Rahul was seeking “regime change with foreign help” and acting on behalf of foreign powers seeking instability in the country.Union minister Kiren Rijiju also took an indirect swipe at the Congress over the involvement of foreign political figures in India's domestic affairs.Reacting to the controversy in a post on X, he wrote, “Have you ever seen anyone laughing when India is insulted by a foreigner? I'm not asking about which Indian goes abroad to insult India.”Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao had also criticised Rahul’s remarks on democracy at the summit and demanded an apology.Referring to the Raebareli MP's statement that democracy had been destroyed in India since 2014, Rao cited the Emergency and the dismissal of elected state governments during Congress rule.The Bharat Summit 2026 has brought together around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries to discuss global geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.
Article Summary: Deborah Bergamini is a member and national deputy secretary of Forza Italia, a centre-right political party that is part of the governing coalition supporting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. She criticised Giacomo Filibeck, secretary general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), over his “Vote thieves, step down from your seats” remark targeting the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Article Title: 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for upcoming UP elections
Article Text:
The BJP said its candidate selection process for the 2027 UP polls has not yet begun and dismissed the reports as fabricated

NEW DELHI: The Uttar Pradesh unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Sunday rejected reports claiming that a list of 209 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections had been prepared and sent to the party's central leadership, calling them fabricated and part of a "well-planned conspiracy"."For the past few days, certain media outlets, individuals, and institutions have been continuously circulating news regarding an alleged list of 209 candidates of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Uttar Pradesh, being prepared and sent to the central leadership in the context of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. This is completely untrue, baseless, imaginary, and fabricated. The BJP outrightly refutes this fake and false news," news agency ANI quoted the statement as saying.Describing the reports as a "well-planned conspiracy", the statement alleged that some people were spreading rumours to create confusion, uncertainty and fear among party workers. It urged office-bearers, workers and the public not to rely on unverified reports and to follow information shared through authorised party platforms.The party said its candidate selection process had not yet begun. It added that the BJP follows a structured organisational process for choosing candidates for assembly and other elections.The joint statement was signed by chief minister Yogi Adityanath and state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary.Earlier on Sunday, Chaudhary had also denied that the BJP had finalised names for 209 constituencies. Speaking to reporters, he said he had not held any meetings to prepare such a list.“I do not know the source of this news... As the State President of the Bharatiya Janata Party, I have not held any such meetings with anyone,” Chaudhary said.He outlined the party's candidate selection procedure, saying inputs are first collected at the district and regional levels before being discussed by the state core committee and election committee. The recommendations are then sent to Delhi, where the Parliamentary Board takes the final call.“The BJP is not a family-run party where a single individual can make such decisions; rather, the process is entirely collective,” he said.Chaudhary added that the party had followed the same organisational approach for the past 50 years, with decisions taken through consultation and consensus.
Article Summary: The Uttar Pradesh unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Sunday rejected reports claiming that a list of 209 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections had been prepared and sent to the party's central leadership. The party said its candidate selection process had not yet begun.

NEW DELHI: Kishtwar BJP MLA Shagun Parihar criticised J&K authorities over the handling of the mortal remains of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) killed in Kishtwar district. She alleged that their bodies were brought to the area in a dumper truck and handled with indignity."You brought the bodies of our people here in a dumper truck... Is this the value of our jawans?" She also questioned why senior officials had not responded sooner to the families' concerns."It has been three days... Both were residents of Kiyar Dachhan and were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) in the Kiyar sector.The two SPOs had gone missing on November 10 while travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah for rotation duty. NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gang rape and murder case and granted them bail."Having heard the parties, suffice it to state that the appellants have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law," the apex court said in its October 28 order that has now been uploaded."In view of the above and considering the issues involved in this appeal, we suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellants on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court," the bench added.A Supreme Court bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale noted that Bilkis Bano case convicts Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya had spent more than 17 years in prison.The two are among the 11 convicts whose remission was quashed by the apex court on January 8, 2024. Bano was five months pregnant when she was gang-raped during the 2002 Gujarat riots , while her three-year-old daughter and six other family members were killed.The other convicts in the case are: Govind Nai, Ramesh Chandana, Mitesh Bhatt, Bakabhai Vohania, Kesarbhai Vohania, Jaswant Nai, Radheshyam Shah, Rajubhai Soni and Shailesh Bhatt.The court had earlier struck down the Gujarat government's remission order, holding that Maharashtra had the authority to decide on their early release.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gang rape and murder case and granted them bail. Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya had spent more than 17 years in prison. Bano was five months pregnant when she was gang-raped during the 2002 Gujarat riots.

NEW DELHI: Security forces defused three grenades found inside a polythene bag in the Durhama area of north Kashmir 's Baramulla district, news agency ANI quoted officials on Monday.The recovery comes days after Baramulla Police arrested a man and seized two hand grenades from the Baderkoot forest area of Tangmarg in Jammu and Kashmir.The arrested man was identified as Ghulam Jeelani Reshi, a resident of Baderkote in Tangmarg. A political row has erupted over the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district. BJP leader Sunil Sharma has accused Congress's state chief Tariq Hameed Karra of spreading misleading information about the incident that could be used by Pakistan's propaganda machinerySharma, the leader of opposition in the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly, accused the Congress of attempting to shift the blame for the killings from terrorists to security forces. His remarks came after Karra called for a thorough investigation into claims that the two SPOs may have been shot by security personnel who mistook them for militants.Speaking to reporters in Srinagar earlier on Sunday, Karra said the killing of the two men on Thursday was condemnable, regardless of who was responsible, but that questions surrounding the incident needed to be answered.“The Kishtwar incident is condemnable, whoever may have committed it. However, many questions are being raised about it,” he said.Rejecting the possibility that the SPOs were killed in a case of mistaken identity, Sharma said Rashpal Kumar and Babi Chand were on duty with the Special Operations Group (SOG) and were travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve personnel stationed there.“They were not out hunting, as Karra claimed. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families,” Sharma said.He also claimed that the terrorists who killed the two men took away their rifles, magazines and ammunition. Sharma cited the recovery of Pakistani-origin armour-piercing cartridges and said Jammu and Kashmir police had issued posters of three wanted terrorists, announcing a reward of Rs 30 lakh.Sharma questioned how the Army could have mistaken the two SPOs for militants, arguing that they were familiar personnel who regularly moved between police and Army posts. He also claimed that Karra's account was inconsistent, saying the Congress leader had acknowledged that the SPOs passed two security pickets without difficulty.The BJP leader also accused Karra of contradicting his own earlier remarks. Sharma said that on November 14, the Congress leader had cited the killings as evidence of terrorism, but raised the possibility of security personnel being responsible a day later.“Spreading hearsay on a terror killing is not politics, it is irresponsibility,” Sharma said, alleging that the Congress's remarks could be used by Pakistan's propaganda machinery to target the Indian Army.He demanded that Karra withdraw his statement and apologise to the families of the deceased, the Jammu and Kashmir police and the Army. Sharma also asked the Congress leadership to clarify whether it supported the security forces or Karra's allegations.Karra, in his remarks, had called for an investigation into the claims rather than declaring who was responsible for the killings. The circumstances surrounding the deaths remain a matter for the investigation.
Article Summary: BJP leader Sunil Sharma accuses Congress's state chief Tariq Hameed Karra of spreading misleading information about the incident. Karra called for a thorough investigation into claims that the two SPOs may have been shot by security personnel who mistook them for militants. Sharma rejects the possibility that the SPOs were killed in a case of mistaken identity.

NEW DELHI: Gauhati high court described the expulsion of expulsion of foreigners in Assam as "very grim picture" and noted that 1,16,946 declared foreign nationals are yet to be apprehended and expelled/A division bench of Justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Mridul Kumar Kalita dismmissed a writ petition related to the expulsion of a declared foreigner on November 10.In its order, the bench cited an affidavit filed by the Assam government, which stated that 1,16,946 declared foreign nationals were yet to be apprehended and expelled."It shows a very grim picture when it comes to the expulsion of foreigners and declared foreign nationals in the State of Assam," the court observed.The petition was filed by Hamida Begum, a resident of Charaideo district, who was declared an illegal foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal in December 2018. She challenged the tribunal's order before the high court, which dismissed her petition in October 2020.She then moved the Supreme Court , which rejected her plea in November 2025. Her review petition was also dismissed in March 2026.Following her detention, Begum was lodged at the transit camp in Goalpara, earlier known as a detention camp.She was released on bail as per the law laid down by the Supreme Court on being detained for three years in a row upon declaration of being a foreign national.However, the high court noted that she was taken into custody again while appearing before the concerned police station, as required after her release.Her counsel approached the high court seeking bail and her release from detention.Dismissing the plea, the bench noted that Begum had exhausted all legal remedies to challenge the Foreigners Tribunal's opinion and had failed to secure relief from both the high court and the Supreme Court.The court further observed that the state was contemplating her expulsion and had taken all necessary steps towards it."Therefore, the state is now contemplating expulsion of the petitioner... the state has taken all necessary steps for the expulsion of the petitioner, and therefore, the present writ petition is not maintainable, nor is the petitioner entitled to bail," the bench said.
Article Summary: Gauhati high court dismmissed a writ petition related to the expulsion of a declared foreigner. The petition was filed by Hamida Begum, a resident of Charaideo district. She was declared an illegal foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal in December 2018.

NEW DELHI: The Central Reserve Police Force ( CRPF ) on Sunday withdrew a battalion of more than 1,000 personnel from Chhattisgarh's anti-Naxal operations theatre and moved it to Manipur to strengthen security deployment amid continuing ethnic violence in the state.The move marks the first complete withdrawal of a Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) battalion from the anti-Naxal theatre since the Centre declared the end of armed Maoism in the country in March.The battalion was stationed in Sukma district, part of the south Bastar region that was once a major Maoist stronghold. It had been involved in Left Wing Extremism (LWE) operations for several years and was subsequently engaged in de-mining and defusing improvised explosive devices (IEDs) after March, news agency PTI reported citing officals.“The CRPF headquarters has ordered the de-induction of a general duty battalion from Chhattisgarh and directed it to move to Manipur, where ethnic violence has been simmering for more than three years now. This is the first full withdrawal of any paramilitary unit from the anti-Naxal operations theatre following the declaration that armed Maoism in the country ended in March,” news agency PTI quoted a senior security officer based in Delhi as saying.The force had deployed two battalions of its specialised jungle warfare unit, the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA), in Manipur a few months ago. Other regular CRPF units and the Rapid Action Force (RAF) have also been stationed in the state.The latest deployment comes with logistical and accommodation challenges for security personnel. Officials said instructions have been issued to ensure suitable arrangements for the incoming battalion. Manipur has witnessed a significant deployment of security forces since ethnic violence broke out in May 2023.The CRPF has been the lead central force in anti-Naxal operations, with more than one lakh personnel deployed for the task. Its presence in Chhattisgarh, once the most violence-affected theatre of Left Wing Extremism, included over 25 regular and CoBRA battalions.

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Quad leaders' summit in Manila, a senior US official dismissed as fake news a media report that said the informal strategic and diplomatic partnership involving Australia, India, Japan and the US was withering under the Donald Trump administration.Quad leaders will meet in the Philippines capital on Tuesday after a gap of two years, looking to boost cooperation in maritime security, critical and emerging technologies, climate, health and economic security, along with infrastructure and connectivity.Assistant secretary of state Dylan Johnson described as an utterly ridiculous take a report by Politico that quoted an anonymous Washington-based Asian diplomat to say that Quad was on life support."Secretary Rubio has formally met with the Quad foreign ministers five times in the past two years - with three meetings in the past six months. CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has suspended five library officials over the procurement of AI-generated books for the Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore.According to an announcement made by school education minister A Rajmohan on Sunday, those suspended are S Kamatchi, chief librarian, Anna Centenary Library (ACL), Chennai; Dinesh Kumar, chief librarian and information officer (in-charge), Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai; V Santhanakrishnan, librarian and information officer, Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai, and in-charge of the Periyar Arivulagam Library; S Santhana Karthikeyan, librarian and information officer, ACL, Chennai; and J Juliet, chief accounts officer, Directorate of Public Libraries.The minister said the irregularities had occurred during the previous DMK regime.The alleged irregularities came to light after writer Perumal Murugan identified nearly 1,800 books from Agal Vilakku Pathippagam in the library’s fourth-floor Tamil section.The books reportedly carried inflated prices, AI-generated misinformation, fictitious author names and invalid International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).Writers and researchers subsequently flagged similar irregularities elsewhere.Researchers have also raised concerns about the library’s English-language books. BALLIA: A 28-year-old police sub-inspector died by suicide on a railway track here, allegedly after being blackmailed by a woman, an officer said on Sunday.The sub-inspector, identified as Sandeep Kumar, was posted at the Chitbarhagaon police station in Ballia, news agency PTI reported.SP Iraj Raja said police received information on Saturday night, between 7pm and 8pm, that a person had died by suicide by lying on a railway track.The information was mentioned in an MRO report filed by a railway loco pilot at the next station. Article Title: UP horror: 3 siblings returning from Haryana killed as pickup hits bike, brick-laden tractor runs them over amid dense fog

LUCKNOW: An 18-year-old teenager and his two sisters, aged 18 and 19, were killed after their motorcycle was hit by a speeding pickup vehicle and subsequently run over by an overloaded, brick-laden tractor-trailer amid poor visibility in Sitapur district early Sunday morning.The accident occurred around 6am near a petrol pump in the Rihar area under the Tambaur police station limits.Dense fog and low visibility reportedly reduced visibility on the road, leaving little room for the victims to escape the impact of the collision. All three died on the spot.The deceased were identified as Shishupal, 18, son of Tuka Ram, and his sisters Pooja Devi, 19, and Gayatri Devi, 18. All three belonged to Devpalpur village in the Tambaur area of Sitapur.According to information, the siblings had gone to Haryana to work as labourers and returned to Laharpur late Saturday night.Two residents of their village had reportedly reached Laharpur on separate motorcycles to receive them. On Sunday morning, Shishupal took both his sisters on his motorcycle and set off for their native village.However, when they reached near a petrol pump in Rihar, a speeding pickup allegedly rammed into their motorcycle amid the poor visibility.The impact threw all three onto the road. Before they could move to safety, an overloaded tractor-trailer carrying bricks ran over them, leaving them with fatal injuries.According to local residents, none of the three siblings was wearing a helmet at the time of the accident.The incident triggered panic in the area, with residents gathering at the spot after seeing the bodies lying on the road. The police were alerted and reached the scene shortly afterwards.The police took custody of the bodies and sent them for post-mortem examinations to complete the necessary legal formalities.Tambaur station house officer Pradeep Singh said the police were searching for the tractor-trailer and its driver.Further action would be taken after tracing the vehicle and establishing the circumstances leading to the accident.
Article Summary: An 18-year-old boy and his two elder sisters tragically died in a collision in Sitapur district early Sunday morning. Dense fog and low visibility reportedly reduced visibility on the road, leaving little room for the victims to escape the impact of the collision. All three died on the spot.

LUCKNOW: A 26-year-old man allegedly stormed into a woman’s house and stabbed her, her mother and grandmother following a dispute over her impending marriage to another man in Bahraich late Saturday night.The accused, identified as Arzaan Qureshi, 23, was arrested by the police, Superintendent of Police Vishwajeet Srivastava told TOI.All three women sustained serious stab injuries and were rushed to the district hospital. The condition of the woman, who had earlier lodged a molestation and harassment complaint against the accused, was stated to be critical.According to the SP, Arzaan and the woman had been in a relationship since 2016. He was reportedly angry after learning that her marriage had been fixed with someone else, which allegedly triggered the attack.The incident took place around 11pm in the Dargah police station area of Bahraich city.According to preliminary information, the woman had lodged an FIR against Arzaan around six years ago on charges of molestation and harassment.A case had also been registered against him under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.He was arrested in connection with the case and subsequently released on bail, after which he reportedly left the area.Police said Arzaan arrived at the woman’s house late Saturday night and knocked on the door while disguising his voice. When the woman’s younger sister opened the door, he allegedly pushed her aside and forcibly entered the house.He then attacked the woman with a knife. When her mother and grandmother rushed to intervene and rescue her, the accused allegedly attacked them as well, leaving all three seriously injured.Hearing their screams, neighbours rushed to the house, but the accused had already fled. Local residents subsequently arranged for the injured women to be taken to the district hospital for treatment.Following information about the incident, city circle officer Narayan Dutt Mishra and Dargah station house officer Amitendra Singh reached the hospital and took stock of the situation.Confirming the earlier case against Arzaan, CO City Narayan Dutt Mishra said a molestation case, along with provisions of the POCSO Act, had been registered against him six years ago.The SP subsequently confirmed to TOI that Arzaan had been arrested. Article Summary: A 26-year-old man allegedly stormed into a woman's house and stabbed her, her mother and grandmother following a dispute over her impending marriage. Article Title: Security agencies, dog squad launch hours-long search after caller warns of blast at Mumbai's CSMT station

MUMBAI: A major security operation was launched at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Saturday evening after authorities received a phone call warning of a bomb blast at the busy railway station. The threat, however, turned out to be a hoax after an extensive search of the premises.According to officials, the Government Railway Police (GRP) Control Room at Wadi Bunder received information around 6.40pm about a caller claiming that an explosive device had been planted at CSMT.Following the alert, multiple security agencies swung into action and initiated a comprehensive combing operation across the station.Teams from the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Government Railway Police, Mumbai Police and other security units carried out a coordinated search of the station complex.An RPF dog squad was also deployed to scan key areas, including suburban and long-distance train platforms, foot overbridges and the parcel office.Security personnel thoroughly checked parked trains and various sections of the station to ensure passenger safety.The operation continued for several hours amid heightened vigilance, though railway services were not disrupted.Central Railway chief spokesperson Swapnil Nila said that no suspicious object, explosive material or suspect individual was found during the search.Following the exhaustive sweep, officials declared the bomb threat a hoax.Authorities are now working to trace the caller and determine the source of the threatening message.They reiterated that strict action would be taken against those responsible for creating panic and misusing emergency response systems.
Article Summary: A bomb threat was reported at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Saturday evening. Authorities received a phone call warning of a bomb blast at the busy railway station. The threat, however, turned out to be a hoax after an extensive search of the premises.

JAISALMER: The conspiracy behind the November 3 blast on a railway track near 50 GB village in Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district was allegedly masterminded by a Pakistan-based ISI handler identified as Shah, who used a romantic relationship to recruit a young woman to carry out the attack.The accused were allegedly paid Rs 2.23 lakh for executing the operation, including Rs 1 lakh in cash, while the remaining amount was transferred to their bank accounts.The primary objective behind the railway track blast, allegedly orchestrated by the ISI, was to spread terror across Rajasthan, particularly in Sri Ganganagar.ADGP ATS Dinesh MN, along with senior officials of AGTF, ANTF, Bikaner Range IG Om Prakash and Sri Ganganagar SP Harishankar, disclosed details of the investigation at a press conference on Sunday.The Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Sri Ganganagar police, with assistance from Punjab Counter Intelligence, arrested two accused, including 21-year-old Mahakdeep Kaur and Davinder Singh (23), from Gurdaspur in Punjab.Police recovered two foreign-made pistols, 46 live cartridges and Rs 30,000 in cash from the arrested accused.Dinesh MN said the blast was carried out at the direction of a foreign-based handler whose objective was to spread panic in Sri Ganganagar and across Rajasthan.The handler allegedly provided the target location, funding and instructions for executing the attack.Investigations revealed that Mahakdeep Kaur had married around two years ago, but her marriage ended in December 2024. In February 2025, her husband, Karanveer Singh, was jailed in an NDPS case. Subsequently, he re-established contact with her and allegedly asked her to communicate with a Pakistan-based person named Lovely, who would provide money to be delivered to him in jail.Lovely later introduced her to another person identified as Shah. Gradually, conversations between Mahakdeep and Shah developed into a romantic relationship, and she became emotionally attached to him. The Pakistani handler allegedly exploited this relationship to recruit her for the railway blast and assign her targets.According to the ADGP, Mahakdeep and Davinder visited the Ramsinghpur area on October 6, but their first attempt failed because explosives were not available. Following further instructions from Pakistan, they allegedly succeeded in triggering the explosion near 50 GB on November 3. Investigators are also examining whether a train was the intended target.The breakthrough came after an extensive investigation involving the analysis of nearly five lakh call records and the questioning of more than 400 people. Police also examined suspected Pakistan-linked smugglers and their local contacts before tracing the accused through technical surveillance and human intelligence.Dinesh MN said inputs from central agencies received three days ago led ATS teams to Punjab. With assistance from Punjab Counter Intelligence, the suspects' locations were traced to Gurdaspur, where they were arrested on November 15.Both accused will be produced before a court and taken on remand for further interrogation to identify other members of the network and establish links with Pakistan-based handlers.
Article Summary: The primary objective behind the railway track blast, allegedly orchestrated by the ISI, was to spread terror across Rajasthan, particularly in Sri Ganganagar. Mahakdeep Kaur had married around two years ago, but her marriage ended in December 2024.

Article Title: US flight chaos continues: 2,400 flights cancelled, 8,800 delayed as recovery drags on
Article Text:
US flight chaos enters third day, over 10,000 flights hit

One router, a chain of problems: What went wrong

FAA still has no clear answer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US flyers had to face another day of long waits and disrupted travel on Sunday, as more than 10,000 flights remained cancelled or delayed for the third day in a row.While airlines raced to get their schedules back on track, transportation secretary Sean Duffy said that things could return to normal by Monday (local time).The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is yet to identify the exact cause, even as the incident has renewed concerns about ageing technology and the need to upgrade the country's air traffic systems.The disruption continued to affect airlines across the country on Sunday. According to aviation data site FlightAware, more than 2,300 flights were cancelled and around 7,700 delayed.Saturday was even worse, with airlines cancelling more than 6,400 flights and reporting over 8,000 delays, according to Reuters.JetBlue saw the highest cancellations on Sunday, with 28% of its flights affected. American Airlines cancelled 17% of its flights, while United Airlines, Southwest and Delta reported cancellations of 3% to 5%.Speaking on ABC, Duffy said that flights would come "back to normal" on Sunday "but probably fully normal" on Monday.He also stressed that keeping passengers safe remained the FAA's priority.The trouble started with maintenance work involving routers used by the FAA. According to officials, the installation of at least one new router by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility led to a huge flow of data at other air traffic control centres, affecting their communication systems.Duffy said the replacement of a router at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered problems with a recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas. The Amarillo router began broadcasting, causing other routers at air traffic control centres across the country to become overloaded.The FAA said on Sunday that it had disabled the "functionality of the originating routers". It also took the same step for around 60 similar routers used in the air traffic control system.However, the exact reason behind the failure remains unclear. Duffy said the maintenance work had been carried out thousands of times in the past without any problems.The worker who installed the router was not suspected of deliberately causing the disruption.The worker was "a good American patriot, we believe, a veteran — so we don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install," Duffy said. "But we don't actually have the root cause."Duffy also said the routers that experienced problems were bought in 2001 and had become outdated by 2006.The technical failure led the FAA to issue a nationwide ground stop on Friday, bringing nearly all departing flights to a halt for almost five hours.It was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks on the United States.Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or any other deliberate attempt to disrupt the system. However, the FAA is still trying to establish what caused the failure.The incident has once again highlighted the challenges facing the US air traffic control system. It has been struggling with ageing technology, equipment and communication problems, along with a shortage of several thousand air traffic controllers.The flight disruptions have added urgency to the debate over modernising the country's air traffic control system.Duffy has called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade the infrastructure, raising his earlier demand of $30 billion. This is in addition to the $12.5 billion approved by Congress last year.US President Donald Trump also called for more funding on Sunday, making his first public comments on the weekend's air travel disruptions."We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," Trump wrote on social media. "Congress must approve."But the demand for more money has not gone unchallenged. US Representatives Rick Larsen and André Carson, the top Democrats on the House of Representatives Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and its aviation subcommittee, respectively, questioned why additional funds were needed.
Article Summary: More than 10,000 flights cancelled or delayed for third day in a row. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said things could return to normal by Monday. The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration is yet to identify the exact cause.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: After pointing to commerce secretary Howard Lutnick for Nvidia chips, treasury secretary Scott Bessent has ‘dramatic shakeup’ message for the company
Article Text:
The document drew on surveillance of Alice Huang and an investigation into alleged chip smuggling involving her company, Singapore-based Megaspeed (Photo: AP).

Bessent points to Lutnick

Lawmakers want answers from Lutnick too

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Export controls : Bessent says no new law needed

US treasury secretary Scott Bessent says Nvidia needs a “dramatic shakeup” in leadership after the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang. He also wants answers from the company’s board within 10 days about accusations that the chipmaker helped send advanced AI chips to Chinese entities. Bessent made the remarks on Fox News’s Sunday Morning Futures. He suggested that Nvidia’s board should look outside the company for a new leader. Bessent’s comments came soon after he singled out commerce secretary Howard Lutnick for inaction in putting Megaspeed International on a trade blacklist.“As the board conducts a search for a new leader, they need to go outside the company,” Bessent said, as per Bloomberg. He added that what was going on inside Nvidia means the company needs a dramatic shakeup. He also noted he wants to know whether Nvidia deliberately ignored warning signs that shell companies, many of them in Singapore, were sending chips to China. His comments suggest he wants to move attention away from Huang’s personal “foibles” and toward the legal and national-security side of the story.“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia,” he said, asking whether the company had pushed seemingly illicit sales to boost its revenues and earnings.“I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel,” he said. Bessent said Nvidia has brought in outside counsel. He expects an explanation of what he called a culture of noncompliance at the company.The Treasury chief said he has long supported putting Megaspeed International on a trade blacklist. He pointedly named Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as the cabinet official who would have to act. “Many other departments were pushing for this, and Commerce had the pen,” Bessent said on Sunday (November 15).Lutnick’s oversight of chip exports and controls has faced growing scrutiny since Huang was ousted from Nvidia on Thursday (November 12). A spokesperson for Lutnick told NBC News last week that he had agreed to testify before Congress.Democrats are eager to hear from Lutnick, as per Bloomberg. Representative Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence panel, spoke on CBS’s Face the Nation. He said it looks as if Lutnick has been the barrier inside the government to stopping the flow of Nvidia chips to China. “And the question is why?” Himes asked. He said it is the Commerce secretary’s job and the president’s job to stop that.Republican Representative John Moolenaar is one of three House committee chairmen seeking testimony from Huang. He said Lutnick and the entire Commerce Department need to answer questions as well.Moolenaar chairs the committee on China’s strategic rivalry with the US. He also suggested Huang should have known that “every Chinese national” can be pressured to spy by the Communist Party. He called that failure “simply irresponsible and a direct threat to our national security.”Lawmakers are pressing Nvidia and the Trump administration for more information on whether they have done enough to keep AI chips out of China. Congress is rallying behind bipartisan export-control legislation that would limit China’s access to AI chips and chipmaking equipment. It could pass within weeks.Bessent rejected calls for such a law, including from Democrats, who will hold majorities in both chambers of Congress from January. “I don’t think we need the legislation. We have all the rules we need. We just need them enforced,” he said.
Article Summary: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent says Nvidia needs a ‘dramatic shakeup’ in leadership after the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang. He also wants answers from the company’s board within 10 days about accusations that the chipmaker helped send advanced AI chips to Chinese entities.

Article Title: A hotel in Germany reports Chlorine gas poisoning after email warning system fails due to Microsoft 365 outage; guests taken to hospital
Article Text:
Representative Image

Microsoft's longest outage

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The recent 24-hour-plus Microsoft cloud outage reportedly prevented an automated safety system from alerting staff to a chemical malfunction at a German theme park hotel. The incident led to a Chlorine gas leak that injured 15 people, local broadcaster WDR reported. The incident occurred in the pool and sauna area of the Hotel Ling Bao at the Phantasialand theme park in Bruhl. According to emergency services, a defect in the pool’s automatic dosing system caused excessive amounts of chlorine to be pumped into the water, triggering a hazardous gas leak.The facility’s maintenance safety system is designed to monitor chemical levels and notify staff of irregularities via email. However, when the system attempted to dispatch a warning regarding the surging chlorine levels, the Outlook message failed to arrive due to widespread disruptions affecting Microsoft’s Exchange cloud infrastructure. Without the automated alert, the chemical buildup went undetected until guests and staff began experiencing symptoms.A total of 40 first responders were reportedly dispatched to the scene. According to the local fire department, 15 individuals suffered respiratory irritation and required emergency triage.Four people were transported to nearby hospitals for further treatment, with one patient remaining hospitalized under observation. Subsequent testing by emergency crews confirmed that the malfunctioning dosing mechanism had pushed the pool's chlorine concentrations to dangerously high levels.Microsoft outage, reports of which started climbing around ⁠1725 GMT on November 12 according to Ookla, is one of the longest in the company's history. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual ​meetings. As Microsoft Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. Microsoft said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online — its cloud-based email and ​scheduling hub — leaving unconnected applications operational.The outage affected government agencies from Australia and Japan to the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to ​public statements. Downdetector logged more than 7.4 million reports worldwide, peaking at nearly 20,000 a minute, more than 1,500 times normal levels.This was the second big outage for the company this year. Microsoft also faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and in ‌ October last year. Last ⁠month, it reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software and a range of industries worldwide.
Article Summary: Microsoft cloud outage reportedly prevented automated safety system from alerting staff to chemical malfunction at German theme park. The incident led to a Chlorine gas leak that injured 15 people, local broadcaster WDR reported. Microsoft outage is one of the longest in the company's history.

Article Title: SC review of 2-child norm puts women’s rights, unintended consequences in focus
Article Text:
Image used for representative purpose.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





DEHRADUN: When Tabassum Parveen decided to contest the 2019 Panchayat elections in Uttarakhand, she was entering electoral politics for the first time after retiring from a govt job. She wanted to become gram pradhan of Kedarawala, but having three children threatened to stand in her way.Following petitions challenging the two-child eligibility provision in Uttarakhand high court (HC), the state introduced July 15, 2019, as the cut-off date, allowing those with third child born before that date to contest. Tabassum, whose youngest child was born in 2017, became eligible and went on to win the election.Her case highlights how a cut-off date on childbirth can determine whether someone gets to participate in grassroots democracy.The provision has come under renewed scrutiny after the Supreme Court (SC), on Nov 4, referred its 2003 ruling in Javed vs State of Haryana, which upheld the two-child norm for panchayat elections, to a larger bench for reconsideration. The court questioned the norm’s relevance, noting that India’s TFR had fallen to 1.9, below the replacement level of 2.1, and said the restriction affected political representation and reproductive autonomy.In addition to the demographic argument, the provision has also raised questions about its unintended consequences, particularly for women who may have little control over family-planning decisions. In families where there is pressure to have a male child, women may be pushed into repeated pregnancies, abortions or face abandonment and marital breakdown if they have more than two children, experts said.An official of the Uttarakhand State Election Commission confirmed that disqualifications had taken place under the provision in the state, but said the commission did not maintain statewide figures specifically for this category.In Feb 2026, Nizamabad police arrested a man accused of killing his six-year-old daughter to remain eligible to contest Panchayat elections in his native village in Maharashtra. He had allegedly explored giving her up for adoption and altering her birth records before killing her. Separately, a 2018 Development Alternatives study cited research in Rajasthan documenting sex-selective abortions, children being given up for adoption and remarriage linked to the two-child norm.Rekha Pundir, secretary of Panchayati Raj and Gender Awareness Training Institute (PRAGATI), said she had come across four to five cases in Uttarakhand over the past decade in which women faced difficulties because of the rule, though there could be more. “If a woman has three children, what is her fault? She may not have had a say in the decision to have another child. Sometimes men insist on having more children or keep trying for a son after two daughters. Such women are automatically prevented from contesting elections,” she said.Pundir, who has worked on training elected women representatives in governance, legal awareness and gender sensitisation, argued that population control could not be achieved through such a limited measure. While fewer children can give women more time to pursue careers and participate in public life, she said, their lack of control over family planning often remains invisible.Women’s rights activist and lawyer Renu Singh, however, believes the provision has helped women enter grassroots politics. She argued that fewer childcare responsibilities give women greater scope to pursue public life and decision-making roles. “If you keep a woman occupied with repeated pregnancies and the responsibility of raising children, she will eventually be completely consumed by these responsibilities,” Singh said, adding that the two-child norm should be retained.Acknowledging that women can become instruments in family-planning decisions when they lack economic and social independence, Singh said the solution was not to keep them trapped in repeated pregnancies. “Son preference and women’s lack of social and economic independence need to be addressed separately. Removing the two-child norm is not the solution. These issues require interventions at other levels,” she said.
Article Summary: Tabassum Parveen had three children before becoming eligible to contest election. Uttarakhand introduced July 15, 2019, as the cut-off date. Supreme Court referred 2003 ruling in Javed vs State of Haryana to a larger bench for reconsideration.

Article Title: A US Air Force veteran who loaned his Iraq war helmet to a Wyoming veterans' post spent 11 days in jail after taking it back; prosecutors later dropped the felony theft case when they could not prove
Article Text:
Richard Knapp/Image: Cowboy State Daily

How an Iraq war helmet became the subject of a theft case

Witness statements helped establish ownership

Prosecutors drop felony charge against veteran

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A US Air Force veteran was arrested at an airport and held for 11 days after retrieving a combat helmet he had lent to a veterans' organisation in Wyoming. Prosecutors later dropped the felony theft charge after evidence emerged supporting his claim that the helmet belonged to him.Richard Knapp, 59, was arrested on July 23 at Washington Dulles International Airport while travelling with his wife and three young family members. The family had returned to the United States from the Netherlands to visit his mother and travel to several locations when authorities took him into custody.Speaking to Cowboy State Daily, Knapp said his family had no idea that a warrant had been issued against him. His wife, Nathalie, and the other family members broke down as officers took him away. "We all did," Knapp said, recalling how the family reacted to the arrest.The arrest also raised concerns about his health. Knapp requires anti-rejection medication twice a day after receiving a kidney transplant from his wife three years earlier. He said he was not given the medication while held at the Loudoun Adult Detention Center in Virginia, leaving him worried about the transplanted organ.Eight days after his arrest, Knapp was transferred to Wyoming in a three-day ground journey.He said authorities at the Laramie County jail provided his medication after he arrived in Cheyenne. Describing his experience in custody, he said, "Jail is ... jail." Court records show he was released on August 10 after posting $300 towards a $3,000 bond.Knapp served in the US Air Force for 20 years and eight months, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, according to the news outlet. During his service, he worked as a civil engineer and was assigned to a construction battalion. His advanced combat helmet was part of the equipment he used during his deployment to Iraq.After retiring, Knapp became commander of Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) Post 4343 in Cheyenne, serving from 2015 to 2016. He allowed the organisation to display his helmet in a glass cabinet alongside other military memorabilia.Greg Anderson, who served as a fellow VFW officer during that period, told Cowboy State Daily that members had voluntarily contributed personal belongings to the display and could reclaim them whenever they wanted."All that stuff in that display case was brought in voluntarily by people," Anderson said. He added that members had the right to take their belongings back at any time.The dispute emerged in September last year, when Knapp returned to the post to collect the helmet. According to an affidavit by Laramie County Sheriff's Deputy Erin Gerhardt-Valois cited by the outlet, surveillance footage showed him opening the display cabinet, removing the helmet and attempting to leave through a side entrance. After finding the door locked, he returned to the room, picked up the helmet and left through the bar area with three companions.The incident was reported to authorities as a theft in October that year. David Stewart, the post's quartermaster, told investigators that the helmet was worth approximately $2,600. Knapp disputed the valuation, telling Cowboy State Daily that it was worth less than $400.The difference in the estimates had legal consequences. Wyoming law sets a $1,000 threshold for felony theft, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years. Theft below that amount is generally treated as a misdemeanour, punishable by up to six months in jail.The Laramie County District Attorney's Office filed a felony charge against Knapp on October 20. A warrant was subsequently issued, but Knapp said he remained unaware of it until his arrest in July 2026.The case took a different turn after investigators received statements from people who said they had witnessed Knapp bring the helmet and accompanying goggles to the VFW for display.According to the deputy's report, Knapp's friend Gary Lustgraaf told investigators that the veteran had wanted to retrieve the helmet because the post was undergoing changes and might be closing. Lustgraaf also said Knapp did not intend to take the item to the Netherlands and had left it with him.Anderson and other witnesses also provided accounts supporting Knapp's ownership of the military equipment. Stewart subsequently passed these statements to the investigating deputy on August 4, while Knapp was being transported to Wyoming.Deputy Gerhardt-Valois collected the helmet as evidence and also spoke with Knapp's family about his medical requirements. Her report noted that she contacted jail nursing staff to explain his condition.Laramie County Sheriff Brian Kozak later reviewed the investigation report and told Cowboy State Daily that it provided a complete account of the incident. He also said the deputy had made efforts to assist Knapp during the process.Knapp hired attorney Sara Lock of Just Criminal Law to represent him. He told Cowboy State Daily that he worked with his lawyer to establish the helmet's actual value and provide information supporting his ownership claim.On September 1 this year Laramie County Deputy District Attorney William Edelman filed a motion seeking dismissal of the case, stating that the prosecution could not meet its burden of proof. Circuit Court Judge Sean Chambers approved the request the following day.The dismissal ended the felony proceedings against Knapp after he had spent 11 days in custody and travelled across the country under extradition arrangements.Although the case was dropped, Knapp said the experience had affected him, particularly given his concerns about his kidney transplant and the time spent in detention. He also said he had no intention of returning to the VFW post."I'm glad I was proven innocent," Knapp told outlet. "I would never do anything like (felony theft). Never."
Article Summary: Richard Knapp, 59, was arrested on July 23 at Washington Dulles International Airport while travelling with his wife and three young family members. Knapp served in the US Air Force for 20 years and eight months, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan. After retiring, Knapp became commander of Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) Post 4343 in Cheyenne, Wyoming. He allowed the organisation to display his helmet in a glass cabinet alongside other military memorabilia.

Article Title: 10 platoons, drones, body cams: Bangladesh on alert in Hasina's hometown amid planned return
Article Text:
BGB has deployed 10 platoons, APCs and surveillance equipment in Gopalganj following unrest by Awami League supporters

Bangladesh has deployed 10 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel in key areas of Gopalganj, the hometown of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina . This comes amid heightened security concerns following unrest by Awami League supporters and reports of her planned return in December, the Dhaka Tribune reported on Monday.The deployment includes armoured personnel carriers (APCs), body-worn cameras and drone surveillance to monitor the situation and prevent further violence.The BGB headquarters' media department announced the deployment. It said APCs had also been positioned to deal with any untoward incidents and carry out riot control operations if required.The force has equipped the maximum possible number of deployed personnel with body-worn cameras to monitor their activities. Live footage from the ground is also being collected through drones and other devices, with the BGB headquarters' monitoring cell overseeing the security situation.The deployment has been made under the "In Aid to Civil Power" framework on the directions of the ministry of home affairs. Personnel have been stationed at key locations based on the requirements and advice of the district magistrate, the BGB said.The security build-up follows a show of force by supporters of the banned Awami League in Gopalganj on Sunday.Party activists and members of affiliated organisations took out processions carrying machetes, axes, spears, sticks and oars, according to eyewitnesses and local reports.Despite a heavy security presence, the demonstrators marched through several parts of the district town, reopened the party's district office, vandalised a police vehicle and public installations, and set fire to the July Memorial.Following the unrest, the government transferred Gopalganj's deputy commissioner and superintendent of police.The developments come amid reports of Sheikh Hasina's planned return to Bangladesh in December. Her supporters have stepped up activities in her ancestral hometown following the announcement.

Article Title: 'Bulletproof cabins won't save them': Gangster Goldy Dhillon targets Amitabh, Abhishek Bachchan
Article Text:
Gangster Goldy Dhillon has issued a death threat against Bollywood actors Amitabh and Abhishek Bachchan.

NEW DELHI: Gangster Goldy Dhillon, Lawrence Bishnoi 's close aide, has threatened to kill Bollywood veteran Amitabh Bachchan and his son Abhishek over an alleged, unsubstantiated remark made by the former on the 1984 riots.Dhillon posted on Facebook Monday saying that the recent arrest of two of his associates in Mumbai by the Delhi Police Special Cell will not deter their operations and no bulletproof glass will shield him.In the social media post, Dhillon identified the arrested individuals as Vikas Thakur and Deepak Singh, clarifying that they belong solely to his faction and should not be linked to any other gang.He claimed that their detention has not averted any planned attack and asserted that 200 more of his operatives are stationed and ready in Mumbai.Directly targeting the Bachchan family, Dhillon issued a stark warning stating that no matter how many bulletproof cabins they construct or security measures they adopt, the father-son duo will be killed inside those very enclosures.He explicitly named Amitabh Bachchan and Abhishek in parentheses following the threat.The post further stated that anyone deemed guilty of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots will never be forgiven and will be hunted down regardless of who they are or which country they reside in.Dhillon added that anyone speaking against the Sikh community is considered an enemy of his syndicate.Concluding the message with religious salutations, the post tagged several hashtags referencing the 1984 riots alongside handles associated with his network, including Goldy Dhillon Group, Rana Dhillon, Jagga Tarn Taran, Rocky Portugal, Fouji UK, and Suman Germany.Security agencies are expected to review the threat and assess the security detail surrounding the actors.

MUMBAI: Congress has demanded an inquiry into BMC's Rs 37-crore digital classroom project, alleging that Interactive Flat Panels installed to replace blackboards lack required educational content in several municipal schools and cannot be used for teaching.In a letter to municipal commissioner Ashwini Bhide, Congress corporator and BMC group leader Ashraf Azmi sought penalties against suppliers, an immediate stop-payment order, withholding of pending dues and blacklisting proceedings over the missing content.He also sought intervention and a written action-taken report. Article Title: Traders oppose police order mandating 24-hour CCTV coverage
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
