The District Traders Federation for Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has strongly opposed the police administration’s order making it mandatory for traders to keep CCTV cameras covering up to 50 metres outside their establishments running 24 hours.The federation has objected to the provision that criminal cases may be filed against traders if any lapse is found. The federation’s central argument is that the city already claims to have a Smart City CCTV surveillance network in place, and the burden cannot now be shifted to traders under threat of criminal prosecution.“If the Smart City cameras are already supposed to be watching the city, why are traders being threatened with criminal cases?” asked Laxminarayan Rathi, vice-president of the District Traders Federation.“Crores of public money were spent on this system. First fix that system and take action against the contractor if it is not working, instead of making traders criminals,” he added.According to the federation, crores of rupees were spent under the state govt and Smart City project to install smart cameras across the city, with the claim that the entire city was under surveillance.Their live feed was supposed to be available at the police commissioner’s office, the municipal corporation’s Smart City office, various police stations and the city traffic department.If that system was already in place and functional as claimed, why are traders now being told to maintain 24-hour surveillance at their own cost and face cases for lapses, the federation asked.Rathi said many publicly funded smart cameras were non-functional and sought details of police action, including any case filed against the contractor who installed them. “The Smart City system remained defunct without accountability, while traders who installed cameras at their own expense were being threatened with FIRs,” he said.The Federation said many commercial establishments switch off all electricity supply while closing for safety reasons. “At such times, the cameras also go off. Despite this practical difficulty, the police order now makes it mandatory to keep cameras on for 24 hours and provides for filing cases if this is not done,” Rathi said.Calling the order arbitrary, the federation has demanded that it be stayed immediately and a comprehensive meeting be held to find a way forward with cooperation from all sides and through public awareness.Top police officials could not be reached for their comments.
Article Summary: The District Traders Federation for Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has strongly opposed the police administration’s order making it mandatory for traders to keep CCTV cameras running 24 hours. The federation has objected to the provision that criminal cases may be filed against traders if any lapse is found.

(File pic) A private sleeper bus traveling from Pune to Nagpur crashed into a drain after hitting a bridge railing.

CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A 25-year-old man was killed and 25 passengers injured after a private sleeper bus travelling from Pune to Nagpur plunged into a nearly 20-foot-deep drain/nullah after crashing through a bridge railing on the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar-Jalna highway early Saturday.The bus was carrying 26 passengers, including 14 men, nine women and two children, when the accident occurred. One male passenger sustained critical injuries and died shortly while being rushed to hospital. The remaining passengers suffered injuries of varying degrees, with one reported to be in a serious condition.Personnel from Chikalthana police station of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar rural rushed to the spot after receiving information about the accident. They broke the bus's windows to rescue passengers trapped inside and shifted the injured to nearby hospitals for treatment.The deceased has been identified only by his first name, Sai, a 25-year-old. His body was shifted to the Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) for postmortem examination.Police said that they have contacted his co-workers to establish his identity and inform his family. His full name is expected to be confirmed after his relatives arrive, police said.Satish Devkar of Chikalthana police station said the police had contacted the deceased's colleagues and were coordinating with them to inform his family about the tragedy.The accident led to a major traffic disruption on the busy Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar-Jalna highway, with vehicles piling up on both sides of the stretch.Police diverted traffic through alternative routes and introduced one-way movement to ease congestion.Two cranes were pressed into service to pull the mangled bus out of the drain. Police personnel also cleared debris, scattered material and broken pieces of the bridge railing from the road to facilitate the restoration of traffic.The exact cause of the accident is yet to be ascertained.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old man was killed and 25 passengers injured after a private sleeper bus plunged into a nearly 20-foot-deep drain/nullah after crashing through a bridge railing. The bus was carrying 26 passengers, including 14 men, nine women and two children, when the accident occurred.

Article Title: Latur cop faces action for being inebriated in uniform at Pune railway station
Article Text:

A police assistant sub-inspector from Latur district police, on medical leave, is facing stringent departmental action after he was allegedly found inebriated while wearing his police uniform at Pune railway station. A video showing him asleep at the station went viral on social media, prompting action from the Latur police.Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe, taking serious cognisance of the incident, has initiated departmental proceedings against assistant police sub-inspector Ganpat Gopinath Pawar attached to the Latur police headquarters.Police said Pawar had been on medical leave since Nov 3 and travelled to Pune to visit family during Diwali. During his stay, he was allegedly found under the influence of alcohol at Pune railway station while wearing his police uniform. A video showing him lying asleep on the station premises subsequently surfaced on social media, drawing attention to his conduct.The Latur police control room received information about the viral video and an incident report, after which a preliminary inquiry confirmed that Pawar was inebriated.Tambe said the incident was taken seriously as police conduct in public directly affects the police’s credibility and image."The police uniform represents discipline, responsibility, commitment to duty and public trust. Finding a police personnel in an inebriated condition in public while wearing the uniform is a serious matter. We have initiated stringent departmental proceedings against the concerned assistant sub-inspector as per the rules.Such indiscipline, which brings disrepute to the police force, will not be tolerated," Tambe said.The SP said every officer was expected to maintain the dignity of the uniform and uphold the department’s reputation through responsible conduct.Additional SP Mangesh Chavan said disciplinary standards apply to all personnel, including those on leave, and misconduct that undermines public confidence in the police force would invite strict action.
Article Summary: A police assistant sub-inspector from Latur district police, on medical leave, is facing stringent departmental action. He was allegedly found inebriated while wearing his police uniform at Pune railway station. A video showing him asleep at the station went viral on social media.

Article Title: 'If I have to face this, what about common man?': Maharashtra minister Sanjay Shirsat questions police after attack on his residence
Article Text:
Maharashtra minister Sanjay Shirsat expressed concern over police inaction after three youths caused a disturbance at his residence

CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: "City police commissioner's phone was switched off. What are the police doing?," Maharashtra Social Justice minister Sanjay Shirsat alleged that three youths created a disturbance outside his private residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Thursday night by smashing bottles and attempting to create a ruckus, news agency PTI reported.The incident prompted him to question the city's law and order situation and criticise the local police for their alleged lack of response.Shirsat, who also serves as the district guardian minister, said he had to contact Maharashtra Director General of Police (DGP) Sadanand Date around midnight as he could not reach senior police officials. He claimed that the city police commissioner's phone was switched off and no senior officers were available to respond.Questioning the police response, Shirsat said, "My objection is not to what took place. The issue is, what are the police doing about it? The police commissioner's phone was switched off, and no ACP or DCP was available. At least take cognisance when a guardian minister's house is being attacked,".He also expressed concern over the increasing number of criminal incidents in the city, alleging that murders were being reported in broad daylight and that the police commissioner had failed to demonstrate sufficient seriousness about the situation."If I have to face this, then the question arises about the plight of a common man," the Shiv Sena leader said.Shirsat added that he would raise the matter with chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also holds the Home portfolio, and seek action against the police commissioner over the incident.The incident also drew criticism from opposition leaders, who questioned the Mahayuti government's handling of law and order in Maharashtra.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut shared a video of Shirsat on X and tagged chief minister Fadnavis, urging him to take cognisance of the allegations.Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar also criticised the state government, accusing it of failing to maintain law and order.In a post on X, Wadettiwar alleged that criminals had lost their fear of the law under the Mahayuti government. He further claimed that women and girls were unsafe in the state and questioned the security available even to ministers."If a minister whose residence has been attacked has to express helplessness, saying 'if this is my condition, what about the common people?', who will guarantee the safety of ordinary citizens and women in Maharashtra?" he asked.Wadettiwar added that the incident reflected the deteriorating law and order situation in the state.
Article Summary: Social Justice minister Sanjay Shirsat alleged that three youths caused a disturbance outside his private residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Thursday night. The incident prompted him to question the city's law and order situation and criticise the local police for their alleged lack of response. He claimed that the city police commissioner's phone was switched off and no senior officers were available.

Article Title: Environmentalists & farmers protest against Adani Green Energy Limited’s hydropower project near Tarali
Article Text:
Protesters gather near Tarali dam against Adani’s pumped storage hydropower project

Kolhapur:

AGEL Rejects Charges

Hundreds of farmers, environmentalists and activists from across Maharashtra staged a protest at Adani Green Energy Limited’s (AGEL) pumped storage hydropower project near Tarali dam in Patan taluka on Saturday, alleging large-scale destruction of forests. They warned the project could threaten irrigation supplies for thousands of hectares in western Maharashtra.The protest, led by actor-environmentalist Sayaji Shinde and student leader Vivekanand Patil, drew farmers from Sangli and neighbouring districts who fear the Rs 5,600-crore project will adversely affect water availability from Tarali dam, a key source feeding the Krishna and Arphal canal systems.Maruti Chavan, a grape grower from Palus in Sangli district, said farmers dependent on canal water were already facing shortages. “Our farming depends on water from Tarali dam released into Krishna canal. We are already facing an acute shortage of water. I came to mark my protest since I fear the project would eventually consume huge quantities of water, and there will be shortage for agriculture,” said Chavan.Protesters claimed that thousands of hectares under sugar cane, grape cultivation and dairy farming depend on water released from major dams in Satara district, and feared the hydropower project could affect the region’s agricultural economy.The agitators also accused the company of causing ecological damage in the Sahyadri ranges and alleged that the project’s valuation had been shown at only a fraction of its actual cost to reduce environmental compensation liabilities.“Why are such projects planned in the Sahyadri mountain ranges? These projects cause irreversible damage to the natural wealth. The project has immensely damaged the wildlife ecosystem. Many trees had to be cut. Govt must stop the project immediately,” said Shinde.The proposed pumped-storage project aims to generate around 1,500 MW of electricity. According to company officials, nearly 70% of the work has been completed. The project is designed to channel water through tunnels to generate power before pumping it back to the reservoir for repeated use.Some activists also alleged that govt had agreed to procure power from the project at a higher rate, ultimately burdening consumers with increased electricity bills.Adani Green Energy Limited’s (AGEL) dismissed the allegations, particularly claims that the project cost was deliberately reduced in official submissions.“The allegation that the company sought to revise project costs downwards to diminish statutory obligations is completely misleading. The online proposal in the forest/wildlife portal was solely for site investigation purposes, while the State Board for Wildlife (SBWL) considered total project costs of Rs 5,675 crore.Since the site investigation costs are around 1% of project cost, therefore, clarification of the project of Rs 56.75 crore, representing solely the site investigations and survey costs for the online proposal, was provided. Secondly, the allegation that downward revision was intended to lower conservation costs is false,” an AGEL spokesperson said.The company maintained that the Tarali project is located entirely on private, non-forest land and lies 3.2 km from the Koyna Wildlife Sanctuary, outside the notified buffer zone of the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve.“The project does not cause diversion of any protected areas, any reserve forest or notified ESZ,” the spokesperson said.
Article Summary: Hundreds of farmers, environmentalists and activists from across Maharashtra staged a protest at Adani Green Energy Limited’s (AGEL) pumped storage hydropower project near Tarali dam in Patan taluka on Saturday. They warned the project could threaten irrigation supplies for thousands of hectares in western Maharashtra.

Article Title: KMC faces questions over move to regularise unauthorised constructions in Tawde Hotel area
Article Text:
MVA corporators have decided to take a final stand on the issue at their next meeting, while Mahayuti office-bearers said they would decide on the matter on Sunday

Kolhapur

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





: KMC is facing questions over its apparent move to regularise unauthorised constructions in Tawde Hotel area along Kolhapur-Gandhinagar road, instead of initiating action against them.The civic administration is scheduled to submit a factual report on encroachments at the general body meeting on Monday, triggering allegations that an attempt is being made to provide legal protection to illegal structures. Former corporators have warned of approaching the high court’s circuit bench if the administration proceeds with regularisation in violation of court orders.MVA corporators have decided to take a final stand on the issue at their next meeting, while Mahayuti office-bearers said they would decide on the matter on Sunday.The proposed submission of a factual report has raised questions about the administration’s intentions. Critics have pointed out that the civic body is responsible for acting against constructions that violate development regulations, questioning why it appears to be considering regularisation instead of enforcement—particularly when ordinary citizens face strict action for similar violations.They have also demanded scrutiny of development plan reservations, land use, construction permissions, and other relevant approvals concerning properties in the Tawde Hotel area.Questions have been raised over who will be held accountable if the administration attempts to protect illegal constructions and whose interests are being served by the proposed move.Former corporators, civic body warn of legal actionAnil Kadam, president of the former corporators’ association, has objected to the administration’s reported move and warned that the association would approach the Bombay High Court’s Circuit Bench if any attempt is made to regularise the encroachments.In a representation submitted to mayor Rouparani Nikam and municipal commissioner Rajendra Bharud, Kadam alleged that the administration was preparing to use a state govt letter dated June 24 as the basis for regularising the unauthorised constructions.“Such a move would violate the orders of the high court and Supreme Court. We urge the civic administration not to provide legal protection to the encroachments,” Kadam said.Meanwhile, Baba Parte of All Party Civic Action Committee said, “There should be no attempt to regularise unauthorised constructions on land reserved for green areas, non-development zones, and garbage depots in the development plan, or to give legal sanctity to such structures by changing land use and reservations. Green spaces and lands reserved for public purposes are vital for the environment, public health, and welfare of future generations.It will never be right to sacrifice the public welfare of the entire city to protect the illegal constructions of a few individuals.”The focus is now on the factual report to be presented by the administration at Monday’s meeting, and whether it will recommend regularisation or initiate action against unauthorised constructions.
Article Summary: The civic administration is scheduled to submit a factual report on encroachments at the general body meeting on Monday. Critics have pointed out that the civic body is responsible for acting against constructions that violate development regulations. Former corporators have warned of approaching the high court’s circuit bench if the administration proceeds with regularisation.
